checklist.notes: The language and task demands in the A1-U01-L01 LESSON are broadly appropriate for its declared CEFR tier.
The rule “After he/she, add -s: lives or studies” inaccurately presents studies as simple -s addition; study requires consonant-plus-y → -ies, and third-person-singular scope is wider than he/she.
The reviewed A1-U01-L01 LESSON remains within its declared lesson references and communicative scope.
The answers or static protocol in the A1-U01-L01 LESSON are internally coherent and usable as written.
Most prose is usable, but “Foundational exchange: foundations” is tautological and “Do not add another beat” is an imprecise warning against an added vowel.

No suspiciously distinctive copied passage is apparent in the short A1-U01-L01 LESSON, but internal inspection cannot establish originality beyond the retained project evidence and no Internet-wide comparison was performed.

findings.description: The third-person rule conceals the study → studies spelling change and incompletely identifies third-person-singular subjects.
findings.recommendation: State that he, she, it, and one person or thing take the third-person form; distinguish ordinary -s from consonant-plus-y → -ies.

findings.description: The title is repetitive and “another beat” is less precise than naming an extra vowel sound.
findings.recommendation: Use a specific title and say not to add an extra vowel after final /v/ or /z/.

limitations: This review covers only the immutable A1-U01-L01 LESSON and its fresh static machine-report context. It does not assess human or release approval, provider authentication, live-provider behavior, learner outcomes, or Internet-wide originality.
